The scientists bred mice that were missing most of their cerebral cortexes and then replaced a large part of those missing mouse cells with lab-grown human brain cells. This resulted in mice with human neurons that could be altered to approximate human brain conditions. The technique could potentially create better scientific models for studying neurodegenerative disease.

tech.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
tech.summary: Query optimizers continue to leave much to be desired despite an enormous body of research. A Postgres database should know everything about the stuff that lives in its tables, but the problem is enormously hard. What's not as hard is verifying whether a query plan an optimizer picks is good or not. Language models are particularly good at learning how to do tasks with easily verifiable outputs. A small, open-weights model can be post-trained via supervised fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning to produce Postgres query plans that beat Postgres' default plans.

infosec.title: Chinese Hackers Exploit Critical Tencent Software Flaw for One-Click Code Execution
infosec.summary: China-linked UNC3569 used a single crafted link to gain system-level code execution through Sogou Input Method, Tencent's Chinese-language keyboard app used by hundreds of millions of Windows users, and deployed its GrayRabbit backdoor. Gen Threat Labs found that CVE-2026-51990 chained argument injection in the sgbiz protocol handler with a bundled Chromium 80 browser that was six years out of date, ran without a sandbox, and dropped same-origin protections. Tencent patched the injection bug in version 16.3.0.3498, but the outdated Chromium engine behind the chain remained unchanged as of September 10.

infosec.title: Texas Utility CenterPoint Energy Confirms Data Breach After Hacker Claims 7.49M Records Stolen
infosec.summary: CenterPoint Energy confirmed an attacker pulled customer data through an external-facing API on September 12. A hacker using the alias "4d722e4d656f77" claims 7.49 million records, including names, phone numbers, billing addresses, account numbers, payment status, and partial Social Security numbers. The attacker says the API lacked WAF protection, rate limiting, and JWT/auth tokens, and stopped only after a CAPTCHA was added.

infosec.title: Human Attacker Hits Machine-Speed Exploitation of Marimo RCE
infosec.summary: A human attacker exploited CVE-2026-39987 to achieve pre-authentication remote code execution and harvest cloud credentials from Marimo notebooks. The Sysdig Threat Research Team observed the operator pivot from the vulnerable terminal WebSocket endpoint to an SSH bastion host in eight seconds to access an AWS Secrets Manager SSH key without using large language models. Defenders must focus detection efforts on the shape of the attack chain rather than specific operator fingerprints, because prompt injection traps designed for AI agents failed to identify the human actor.

infosec.title: ParaShells: Parallels Desktop Turns Appliance Install Into a Root Shell
infosec.summary: CVE-2026-90894 lets a non-admin macOS user gain root through Parallels Desktop's appliance installer. JFrog tested Desktop 26.4.0 build 57513 on Apple Silicon. The root daemon exposes a world-writable Unix socket where an unsigned local process can authenticate through PrlSrv_LoginLocal. A quote in sVmParentPath injects tar's --use-compress-program option, and tar then launches an attacker script as root. Parallels released version 27.0.0 on September 1 to fix this issue.

infosec.title: Threat Hunting with JA4/JA4S (+ Practical KQL Queries)
infosec.summary: JA4 is a TLS fingerprint that shows how a client connects, not just where it connects to. Unlike JA3, part of it is readable, so hunters can see the TLS version, SNI, cipher count, and ALPN at a glance. The post includes KQL queries to pull these values from Entra ID sign-ins and Defender network logs, so teams can learn what normal looks like and spot clients that don't match.

infosec.title: The £3 WiFi Extender With a Backdoor in Every Unit
infosec.summary: A £3 Z05L WiFi extender uses an MT7620 chip and a four-megabyte Winbond flash. Its firmware starts Telnet on every boot with root password 198277tt@, and the web API accepts requests without session checks, so a mac parameter can reach system() without validation, allowing root command injection. Firmware updates verify CRC32 values only, allowing forged images, and the firewall leaves inbound services exposed on bridged networks as the config partition stores WiFi credentials in plaintext.

The update also brings Ansible-based certificate automation, composite algorithms for phased post-quantum migration, and SPIRE support for AI agent and workload identities. The platform now runs as a service or on-premises, which matters as DORA, NIS2, and the recent US Executive Order push for CBOM-based inventories.

Josh Gottheimer pushed back and stated that frontier models should instead need to be submitted to the federal government for a short-clocked review cycle before release.

infosec.title: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
infosec.summary: WSO2 API Manager CVE-2026-5430 is under active attack. Forged JWTs using unsupported signing algorithms can bypass authentication and grant administrator access in affected deployments, including API Manager 4.1.0–4.6.0, API Control Plane, Traffic Manager, and Universal Gateway. Captured tokens carried admin privileges, and attackers may access backend endpoints, credentials, consumer keys, application secrets, and internal services.

infosec.title: Reverse-Engineering Find My People to Stalk my ex a Friend, Cause I Can
infosec.summary: An in-depth guide to how the author decided to reverse-engineer Apple's Find My system to register a Linux device and (consensually) track a friend. The author first started by attempting to use the iCloud web API but quickly discovered that it didn't support Find My. After reversing and fuzzing the flow, the author was able to reproduce the process by: authenticating to Apple's private service, registering the Linux machine as an IDS client, receiving the existing Find My share key, and using it to fetch and decrypt the friend's latest location.

infosec.title: Oracle Patches 800+ Vulnerabilities in September 2026 Security Update
infosec.summary: Oracle's September 2026 patch update fixed over 800 vulnerabilities across 17 product families, including more than 100 critical flaws and over 240 exploitable remotely without authentication.

infosec.summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-76461, a 9.8 flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliances.

data.title: How we built LangChain's Paid Media Agent
data.summary: LangChain built a paid-media agent that analyzes campaign data, recommends changes, and applies approved actions, helping paid media reach 20% of its marketing pipeline while cutting qualified lead costs. Its key design principle is to use models for judgment, code for reliable calculations and safeguards, and human approvals for consequential actions.

data.title: How To Run on Three Clouds at Once, and When Not To (45 minute presentation)
data.summary: Form3 runs its payment platform active-active-active across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, treating each provider like an availability zone. Kubernetes, NATS JetStream, and CockroachDB span all three clouds, while custom DNS, networking, and disruption controls preserve quorum. Its US deployment deliberately uses active-standby instead, showing resilience architecture should follow regulatory needs, latency limits, and cost.

data.title: FastRP graph embeddings with Apache DataFusion
data.summary: Graph embeddings turn connected entities into vectors for similarity search, GraphRAG, and graph machine learning, but Node2Vec's random walks create huge intermediate datasets and scale poorly. FastRP replaces that pipeline with iterative neighbor aggregation. A Rust/DataFusion implementation runs out-of-core, matched Node2Vec-level predictive quality in small tests, and processed an eight-million-node graph in about 15 minutes.

data.title: Why your Redis is slow: it is single threaded and you sent it KEYS
data.summary: Redis executes commands on a single thread, so one expensive operation such as KEYS, FLUSHALL, a large DEL, or an unbounded collection read can block every client and cause sudden latency spikes even when CPU and network usage look normal. Use SLOWLOG and LATENCY tools to find offenders, replace full scans with cursor-based SCAN commands, use UNLINK for large deletions, shard oversized keys, and disable dangerous commands in production.

data.title: How Many Labeled Examples Does a Text Classifier Actually Need? I Measured It
data.summary: Before defaulting to an LLM for text classification, benchmark a cheap and near-instant classical model against your available labels, expected volume, and acceptable error rate. In a small support-ticket experiment, TF-IDF accuracy rose from 40% to 60% as training data increased from 2 to 10 examples per category, but intent-based ambiguities remained, suggesting a hybrid approach where LLMs bootstrap labels or handle difficult cases while the classical model processes routine ones.

data.title: Plan Advice in PostgreSQL 19
data.summary: PostgreSQL 19's pg_plan_advice serializes join order, scan type, join method, and parallelism into replayable plan guidance, while pg_stash_advice applies it by query ID. Structural strings make plan diffs stable enough for CI and upgrades, but selective pinning matters: preserving one proven decision is safer than freezing every choice as data distributions and statistics change.

data.title: You don't need to migrate those 300 dashboards
data.summary: Instead of migrating every legacy dashboard, move the trusted metrics, definitions, and business logic that power them. Keep only frequently used dashboards and let AI analytics handle one-off questions using the same governed context.

data.title: Apache Iceberg Python 0.12.0 Release
data.summary: PyIceberg 0.12.0 adds REST-catalog views, conflict-aware commit retries, incremental append scans, Iceberg v3 geometry and geography types, and early use of the File Format API. Correctness fixes cover partition pruning, deletion vectors, manifests, timestamps, and conversions, while Python 3.14 and stronger CI and security support broaden production readiness.

data.title: DuckDB Skills for Claude Code
data.summary: When Claude Code needs to look at a data file, it writes a small Python script, runs it, reads the output, and guesses at column names and types along the way. The DuckDB team's plugin points the agent at the DuckDB CLI instead, so a local file, a remote file, or an Iceberg table behind a login is just a table it can query, with skills for format conversion, object storage, spatial data, documentation search, and session recall.

data.title: Bypassing inference bottlenecks with Retrieve-for-Train
data.summary: Search systems often need a useful set, not ten versions of the same result. They can ask an AI to explore several angles, but generating those searches one by one is slow and expensive. Retrieve-for-Train teaches a smaller model the exploration strategy ahead of time, letting it produce complementary searches together. Google reports broader result coverage with 12-20x lower query-generation latency.

data.title: Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement
data.summary: Airbnb turned a months-long, notebook-heavy process for analyzing support conversations into Insight Miner, an agent harness that encodes extract-embed-cluster workflows, prompt tuning, hard-example mining, and contrastive labeling. Investigations now run in days across languages and geographies, while reproducible traces let experts audit evidence and spend more time on ambiguous samples, hypotheses, and methodological improvements.

data.title: My DuckDB + AI Workflow
data.summary: A simple terminal workflow combining AI agents with DuckDB can handle fast, reliable analysis, data cleaning, and secure access without heavyweight tools or complex semantic layers.

data.title: Let Postgres Enforce Tenant Isolation
data.summary: PostgreSQL row-level security can fail closed beneath EF Core query filters, blocking cross-tenant reads and writes even through raw SQL or attached entities when the application uses non-owner roles and reset tenant context on every pooled connection.

data.title: Pushdown Optimization: Don't Take It for Granted
data.summary: Snowflake and Databricks can place equivalent deterministic filters at very different stages, so predicate pushdown should be verified in execution plans rather than assumed.

design.title: iOS 27 gives Camera app on iPhone three powerful new features
design.summary: iOS 27 introduces major Camera app upgrades, including an AI-powered Siri mode that can understand what the camera sees, customizable camera controls, and exclusive iPhone 18 Pro features like manual aperture and shutter controls, enhanced Photographic Styles, and Apple Reference Image for verifying photo authenticity. The update also makes it easier to personalize the Camera interface by adding or removing controls based on how you shoot.

design.title: For the Designless
design.summary: AI hasn't changed what designers do—it has changed who can attempt design, making creative tools accessible to people who previously lacked the knowledge or budget to create effective visual communication. The key distinction is between users who genuinely benefit from AI assistance, those whose handmade work is more authentic than polished output, and businesses that use AI simply to cut corners, with the greatest value coming from helping underserved users create better, culturally relevant designs through strong visual references. The future of AI-assisted design depends less on generating attractive visuals and more on producing work that reflects local context and authentic visual traditions instead of generic, homogenized aesthetics.

design.title: Six Common Mistakes in Design Tokens Naming
design.summary: Weak design token names slow searches, inflate duplicates, and turn governance into guesswork, according to six recurring naming mistakes design systems teams make. Common pitfalls include naming tokens after components too early, baking current values like colors or pixel sizes directly into names, and reordering name segments inconsistently. Other traps are mixing casing and separators, using vague modifiers like "primary" without defined scope, and renaming tokens without a phased migration and alias strategy.

design.title: Designing with Children, Not for Them
design.summary: A free handbook from Save the Children Finland outlines how to co-design digital products with children rather than for them, through consent, play, and trust-building. Practical techniques include sitting at a child's eye level, using pictures and props instead of direct interviews, and capping group sessions at six children per two adults. Success is measured by how heard a child felt rather than what adults intended, since children lose motivation quickly and need visible, steady progress.

design.title: Native Mac Notch Screen Recorder and Screenshots
design.summary: The fastest way to share what you mean. Record a clip or grab a screenshot, then drag it from the notch into Slack, Mail, or any app.

design.title: The Designer Who Drew Cursor's Icons
design.summary: Marek Minor, founder of Amsterdam studio Minor Adventures, spent a year hand-drawing Cursor's entire icon set of more than 600 icons in two sizes and styles. The set replaced Cursor's inherited VS Code Codicons, with Minor working closely with Head of Design Ryo through explorations like 156 versions of a single hamburger icon. AI helped him think through concepts and build companion tools like a migration dashboard, but he drew every icon by hand and still maintains the set today.

design.title: Product Strategy Starts with What You Will Not Build
design.summary: Product strategy is defined by what a team explicitly refuses to build, not merely a revenue goal paired with a feature list. Marty Cagan calls the choice of which problems to solve the strategy layer sitting above both discovery and delivery, one most companies skip entirely. Three tools do the work: Playing to Win's nested choices, Rumelt's kernel as a fluff detector, and Biddle's Netflix-born DHM, while roadmaps merely sequence the bets.

design.title: How Recent™ gave Spectrum one identity for music, wellness and place
design.summary: Spectrum's refreshed identity is built around three core pillars—Ritual, Pulse, and Body—which are woven into an interlaced "S" logo that symbolizes the festival's blend of music, wellness, and community. The flexible visual system uses a spectrum of purple hues, New Edge 666 typography, abstract gradients and halftones, and a practical pill-shaped information system that adapts seamlessly across signage, merchandise, and digital touchpoints. Rather than relying on clichés of Aruba or festival culture, the brand expresses the island through its content and experiences, creating a premium identity that can shift effortlessly between high-energy nightlife and calm wellness moments.

design.title: How Marie-Lou Garcia turns vacations, friendships and quiet days into serene illustrations
design.summary: Illustrator Marie-Lou Garcia transforms quiet personal moments into serene artwork, encouraging artists to embrace creative freedom, trust their intuition, and stay true to their craft despite industry challenges.

design.title: Canva is Quietly Publishing Nearly 1 Million Websites a Month
design.summary: Canva now publishes close to one million new websites every month.

design.title: The iPhone Duo's Opening Animation is a 10/10 Design Flex for Apple
design.summary: Apple's foldable iPhone Duo debuted an opening animation that blurs the outer screen into the inner display, creating the illusion of glass rather than a phone screen.

marketing.title: These 8 video plays are driving revenue right now
marketing.summary: Don't be sloppy. When others choose AI overload, put people back into every stage of your pipeline. Vidyard's Video in Motion report shows you how the marketing teams that still engage buyers are using video to drive human connection. marketing.title: AI and Google updates to know
marketing.summary: Google is reducing publishers' opportunities to earn search traffic as AI features take up more space. New sports features bring play-by-play updates and fantasy recommendations directly into Search. OpenAI is reportedly restricting some competitor ads in ChatGPT. Meanwhile, 41 of the 50 biggest US news sites saw traffic decline year over year. Several publishers have linked traffic losses to AI Overviews and AI Mode, while some are responding by investing more in direct audiences and reducing reliance on search.

marketing.title: Why activity wins customer engagement
marketing.summary: Traditional ads are losing attention as consumers tune out repetitive, sales-heavy formats. 88% of Gen Z and millennials ignore most ads, while 85% stay loyal to brands that feel genuine. Activity-based campaigns offer a different approach by motivating people to participate rather than simply buy. 65% of consumers say they're more likely to engage with or purchase from brands that motivate people to get active.

marketing.title: LinkedIn carousel sizes you should be testing
marketing.summary: Test 1700×1080 landscape for larger covers, 1200×1500 portrait with bolder text, or two-slide carousels that display at full width. Focus on formats that maximize in-feed visibility and drive engagement with your audience.

marketing.title: AI Search is NOT the same as SEO
marketing.summary: Instead of chasing high-volume keywords, map prompt journeys around the final recommendation a buyer wants, then create content around the decision factors that inform it. LLMs can route users from broad questions to specific recommendations, so owning the highest-volume prompt matters less than being cited for the factors behind the purchase decision. Start with bottom-funnel prompts, map adjacent questions, and build content that answers them.

marketing.title: The Times' Reddit Playbook: What Brands Can Learn - Webinar
marketing.summary: Most brands treat Reddit as a risk to manage. Rachel Duffy, Head of Community at The Times and The Sunday Times, built a different playbook: earning moderator trust, learning subreddit culture, and knowing when to speak up. Join her and Standing on Giants on September 22. SAVE YOUR SPOT →

marketing.title: The New YouTube Opportunity for Agencies (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Agency leaders will discuss some of the newest ways that YouTube can make a brand and their agency successful on YouTube. They'll cover new ad formats and strategies, measurement tactics, and ways to tie advertising campaigns into other YouTube efforts from the brand, including organic and creator initiatives. The free webinar takes place today at 10 AM PT.

marketing.title: Meta One bundles creator and business tools — for a monthly fee
marketing.summary: Meta's new subscription service prices creator and business tools from $2.99 a month for basic app access up to $499 for its top professional tier, with the $49.99 Advanced plan unlocking year-ahead scheduling, bulk uploads, and shared account access without password sharing. Paid tiers also boost visibility directly, through higher search placement and more prominent follow buttons, not just productivity tools. The core apps and Meta AI stay free, and none of the tiers remove ads.

marketing.title: Graphic Designer ≠ Art Director ≠ Creative Director
marketing.summary: Job title confusion runs in both directions. Companies without a creative background borrow a senior-sounding title off a template instead of defining the actual work, while designers themselves inflate titles because freelance clients rarely check credentials. Underneath the confusion, the jobs barely move: a designer executes one piece of visual communication, an art director keeps a whole project's output feeling like one brand, and a creative director sets the point of view behind it. Only company size decides how many people that work gets split across.

marketing.title: The Data Center Water Myth
marketing.summary: Americans are increasingly hearing that AI data centers are draining the country's water supply, but the national scale of the problem is far smaller than viral claims suggest. US data centers consumed about 228 billion gallons of water in 2023, yet that amounted to only 0.015% to 0.2% of total US water withdrawals, compared with 43% for agriculture. A viral claim that every ChatGPT question consumes a bottle of water also misrepresented research that estimated 500 milliliters could be consumed across roughly 10 to 50 GPT -3 responses. Water use can still create serious local concerns, but misinformation and misleading comparisons are turning a site-specific resource issue into a broader narrative about AI infrastructure threatening the US water supply.

marketing.title: Inside the creator economy's AI reckoning
marketing.summary: Creator-economy sentiment toward AI has shifted in about a year from dread to a hunt for leverage, with most creators now treating AI output as a rough starting draft rather than a finished product. That shift is showing up in contracts: some brands now ask for access to creators' AI prompts, while creators are starting to write their own AI-use clauses back to protect their voice. Adoption itself splits by gender, since women are 22% less likely than men to be regular AI users at work and more likely to worry it looks like cutting corners. The recurring conclusion is that audiences still connect to the person behind the work, not the tool that helped make it.

marketing.title: Economists Concerned the AI Bubble Is About to Blow
marketing.summary: Equity and debt issuance are surging, market value is concentrated in a few major tech stocks, and earnings expectations look increasingly unstable.

marketing.title: Perplexity Is Turning Creator Marketing Into a Product Test
marketing.summary: Rather than talking up the brand, creators would review original builds made in Perplexity's own tools, instead of promoting them.

marketing.summary: A guide to how much B2B freelancers are charging in the UK.

crypto.title: Deutsche Bank to launch institutional crypto custody
crypto.summary: Deutsche Bank plans to launch an institutional-grade crypto custody service pending regulatory approval, with a rollout expected later this year. The service will let institutional and corporate clients hold and transfer bitcoin, ether, and select stablecoins, with a roadmap extending into tokenized financial instruments.

crypto.title: Two Robinhood Employees Charged With Insider Trading on Hyperliquid
crypto.summary: Federal prosecutors charged two Robinhood employees with fraud for alleged insider trading conducted on Hyperliquid, the decentralized perpetuals exchange. The employees were allegedly trading perpetual futures on tokens they knew were going to be listed. The activity happened between 2025 and 2026 and netted the pair approximately $50,000 each.

crypto.title: X Launches US Cashtag Program with Brokerage Partners
crypto.summary: X launched its Cashtag Partner Program in the US, converting ticker symbols for stocks, ETFs, and cryptocurrencies into trade entry points within the platform's timeline. Tapping a supported Cashtag surfaces a price chart and related posts, then a "Trade" button routes users to partner brokerages including Interactive Brokers, Moomoo, Gemini, Kraken, and Coinbase. Execution occurs at each brokerage's own app or website rather than within X itself, making this a referral and discovery funnel rather than an in-app trading product. For Gemini, Kraken, and Coinbase, the integration embeds a social-discovery-to-onboarding pipeline directly inside X's financial conversation layer.

crypto.title: Circle launches Arc mainnet with BlackRock and Visa among validators
crypto.summary: Circle opened Arc's public mainnet Wednesday, an EVM-compatible Layer 1 with sub-second finality where gas is paid in USDC, launching with Aave V4, Morpho, and Uniswap among more than 100 applications live from day one. Founding validators including BlackRock, DTCC, ICE, Mastercard, and Visa will join in phases, and Circle and DTCC plan to tokenize DTC-custodied assets on Arc starting in the second half of 2027. Circle also completed the genesis mint of 10 billion ARC tokens this week as a technical milestone, though a public token launch remains undecided as the network plans a move from proof of authority to proof of stake in 2027. Arc ships with Arc Studio, an AI coding agent for smart contracts, and Arc App Kits, an SDK for payments, swaps, onramps, and yield.

crypto.title: Uniswap v4 Hooks Were a Mistake
crypto.summary: 0x Protocol's review of 84,163 Uniswap v4 hooks across six chains found only 19.4% safe, with 54.2% classified as malicious and 26.4% probable malicious, a dataset drawn from routing ~70% of the firm's $42.67 billion in annual volume through Uniswap liquidity. Malicious hooks exploit the gap between quote-time and settlement-time execution, spoofing aggregators and wallets to display one price while delivering up to 50% less at fill. A single hook on Base extracted $143,037 from users across 6,516 trades by charging an 18% median fee on 60.6% of fills. The permissionless design that grants builders custom AMM logic also removes routers' ability to trust quoted prices without independent execution verification.

crypto.title: Falcon Card review: an early spend product, not yet a full neobank
crypto.summary: Falcon Finance's virtual Visa debit card, live since July 20 for KYC-verified users in 90-plus jurisdictions, lets holders spend USDf minted against collateral including stablecoins, major crypto, tokenized gold, and tokenized equities like Ondo's COINon and xStocks' TSLAX without selling the underlying position. The card charges a $0 annual fee and no extra Falcon markup beyond Visa FX charges, and counts spend toward Falcon Miles Season 2, but earns 0% on card balance since yield stays in separately staked sUSDf. It's issued by a third-party EMI rather than Falcon directly, remains virtual-only with no published cashback or ATM fee schedule, isn't a bank deposit or deposit-insured, and blocks Russia, Belarus, China, Singapore, and the US.

crypto.title: L1 Gas Impact: Six Months of Measured Ethereum L1 Gas
crypto.summary: Six months of measured Ethereum L1 execution gas data show plain ETH transfers consuming 13,815 million gas per day, roughly 1.6x more than all Uniswap L1 activity, which ranked second at 8,491 million gas per day. Among rollups posting to L1, Robinhood consumed 665 million gas per day, approximately 2.3x more than Base (271M) and 3.1x more than Arbitrum One (214M), making it the top rollup gas consumer by a wide margin. Order book DEX Lighter's primary instance ranked above both major rollups at 286 million gas per day across 41,184 daily transactions, while smaller rollups including World Chain, Unichain, and Ink each fell below 22 million gas per day. All figures are lower bounds derived from verified direct activity measured through mid-September 2026.

crypto.title: All About x402
crypto.summary: x402 is an open payment specification, originated at Coinbase, that embeds pricing, authorization, and settlement into API workflows, allowing machines and AI agents to pay for calls using stablecoins without OAuth flows or account setup. As delegated purchasing authority expands from narrow API credits to broader agentic decisions, the protocol stands to reshape how APIs, data, and compute are priced and traded between software systems. Cloudflare, AWS, Google, and Fastly are each integrating agent payment capabilities into their existing infrastructure businesses, competing on different layers of the value capture stack. Outstanding questions around data precision, service quality guarantees, trust mechanisms, and payment rail neutrality will determine whether x402 matures into a unified market or fragments across competing implementations.

crypto.title: Testing a EUR deposit on the Anodos card
crypto.summary: A €10 deposit from Wise into Anodos's virtual EUR account arrived within seconds for a fixed €0.90 fee, though spending still requires converting the EUR balance to USD to fund the card since direct EUR spending isn't yet supported.

crypto.title: Erebor Bank's Sweet Stablecoin Deal Backfired
crypto.summary: Erebor Bank offered free USDC and USDT-to-USD conversion at par as a client acquisition tactic targeting crypto firms.

crypto.title: Malaysia ranks among most open Islamic crypto markets
crypto.summary: Fitch Ratings found that Malaysia has become one of the most open Islamic crypto markets globally.

crypto.title: Which card apps grew the most since July
crypto.summary: Looking at install growth across 23 crypto card apps from July to September: Krak roughly tripled from 20,000 to 60,000, Plasma One's Android app launched in July and already reached 50,000, and Bitget Wallet grew from about 110,000 to 150,000.

fintech.title: The only complete, fully configurable AI agent system in financial services
fintech.summary: Train, test, and deploy the only configurable AI agent system built to ensure policy compliance in financial services: Fin . Fin subjects every answer to rigorous, multi-stage validation so it can resolve complex queries with precision. As Lee Burkhill, PM at MonyGroup, says :"I've never seen Fin hallucinate—not once. That's a huge deal. We constantly test it, throw new questions at it, analyze variations and it holds up. That level of accuracy in an AI Agent is rare." Learn more about Fin , the AI Agent making perfect customer experiences possible in 45+ languages.

fintech.title: Mercury launches AI-powered accounting software
fintech.summary: Mercury Books is an AI-powered accounting product that automatically categorizes and reconciles card transactions, invoices, and bill payments, then lets users query their books in plain language through its Mercury Command agent. Customers can use their own accountant or bookkeeper or work with partners like Pilot, Fondo, and Ridgewood, as Mercury expands from banking deeper into accounting and finance operations.

fintech.title: Ramp launches in the UK
fintech.summary: Ramp has officially launched in the UK, bringing its finance automation platform to British businesses as it expands beyond the US. The move opens a major new market for Ramp's corporate cards, spend management, and finance operations products, extending its push to become a global financial operations platform.

fintech.title: Mastercard and Trip.com target travel sector agentic commerce
fintech.summary: Mastercard and Trip.com have joined forces to showcase AI-powered booking experiences for the travel sector. Powered by Mastercard's Agent Suite for Merchants and in partnership with Network International, the organizations are showcasing how consumers will be able to search, book, and complete purchases through Trip.com's AI agent TripGenie.

fintech.title: Enterprise AI is finally delivering on the promise SaaS made
fintech.summary: Primary Venture Partners argues that the strongest enterprise AI companies will win not by owning the best models, but by turning real-world workflow experience into compounding expertise. Their framework centers on “scorebooks” and continual learning loops that capture context, decision traces, expert feedback, and business outcomes, allowing domain-specific applications to improve across customers and build defensibility through workflow ownership, implementation depth, and accountability.

fintech.title: Moats & the Barbell-ification of Software
fintech.summary: AI will erode many traditional software moats by making products cheaper to replicate, migrations easier, and integrations more automated, pushing the industry toward a barbell structure. A smaller number of dominant platforms will try to own entire buying centers through relentless product expansion and scale, while an explosion of tiny, niche software businesses emerges at the other end, leaving mid-sized point solutions increasingly squeezed out.

fintech.title: Why Nasdaq invested $100MM in Kraken at $21B valuation
fintech.summary: The venture arm of Nasdaq announced it is investing $100M into Payward, the parent company behind crypto exchange Kraken, at a $21B valuation. The deal strives to make Kraken a major distribution platform for Nasdaq's tokenized equities, which are set to go live in 2027. This comes as the asset class hit a record $6B in monthly on-chain trading volumes in August.

fintech.title: How certificate-based authentication solves PCI DSS compliance challenges
fintech.summary: Payment and banking infrastructure compliance mandates least-privileged access restricted to the minimum per job function. Siloed audit logs lack the identity context to provide an audit trail without manual work across systems. Teleport offers a guide that explains how certificate-based authentication solves these challenges, and more. Read the guide →

fintech.title: Radical Ventures launches Canada's largest AI fund with $1B first close
fintech.summary: Radical Ventures launched its multi-billion-dollar Radical Breakouts Fund with a first close of more than $1 billion, backed by major Canadian pension funds and banks including CPP Investments, PSP Investments, HOOPP, TD, and BMO. The fund will target late-stage AI companies in Canada and globally, reflecting a push to give Canadian scaleups access to the kind of large private-growth capital that has historically been concentrated in the US.

fintech.title: American Express is building a small-business banking stack
fintech.summary: American Express is expanding beyond cards with a new high-yield Business Savings account, grouping it with Business Checking under a broader “Business Banking” offering. Amex also plans to add Gusto-powered payroll, AI-driven payroll insights, and direct redemption of card rewards into checking, pushing toward a more complete operating account for small businesses rather than just a payments relationship.

fintech.title: Robinhood plans in-kind redemptions and voting rights for Stock Tokens after AMC backlash
fintech.summary: Robinhood plans to add one-for-one share redemptions and voting rights to its Stock Tokens, addressing criticism that the products currently provide only economic exposure without actual shareholder rights. The shift follows backlash from AMC CEO Adam Aron and comes as Coinbase and other tokenization platforms push toward structures that more closely replicate traditional equity ownership, including redemption, dividends, and voting.

fintech.title: Klarna props up new Apple phones
fintech.summary: Klarna is powering Apple's new US device leasing program, including financing for the $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo and $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro, with 12- or 24-month terms that let customers upgrade, buy out the device, or return it. The partnership gives Klarna a major distribution win after failing to land Apple more than a decade ago, while helping Apple push hardware toward a subscription-style model that could encourage more frequent upgrades.

fintech.title: Gulf fintech Tabby clinches $6.5B valuation after latest funding round
fintech.summary: Saudi Arabia-based Tabby raised $233 million in a Series F led by Blue Pool Capital, valuing the BNPL fintech at $6.5 billion, up from $4.5 billion last year. Tabby plans to use the capital to deepen its presence in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, where it is expanding beyond BNPL into larger consumer financing, working capital and cash-account products, while processing more than $18 billion in annualized transaction volume across 25 million registered users.

fintech.title: Grab to buy majority stake in SoftBank-backed Atome for about $1.5B
fintech.summary: Grab agreed to acquire a 60% stake in Atome Financial for $1.49 billion in cash, giving it control of the SoftBank-backed consumer finance company.

fintech.title: Wells Fargo brings international money transfers to mobile app
fintech.summary: Wells Fargo announced the nationwide launch of ExpressSend Mobile, bringing its international money transfer service into the Wells Fargo Mobile app.

it.summary: Ungoverned AI does not wait for your risk program to catch up. It is embedded in software you already license, deployed by teams that never routed it through review, and operating without an audit trail. it.title: Workers are so keen on using AI at work that they're paying for it themselves
it.summary: A Deloitte study found 63% of UK workers have used generative AI for work, while 31% are using it without their employer's knowledge and 17% are personally paying for at least one AI tool. For IT teams, the takeaway is less about stopping AI adoption and more about getting approved tools, training, data controls, and governance in place before shadow AI becomes the default.

it.title: Salesforce hit by global outage as Google Drive also suffers disruption
it.summary: Salesforce suffered a widespread service disruption on September 16 that caused severe delays, intermittent errors, and access problems across regions, with Salesforce attributing the issue to increased load on a core system component. Google Drive separately experienced a 37-minute disruption the same day — a useful reminder of how much employee productivity now depends on a small number of SaaS platforms and why IT still needs outage communications and fallback processes even for highly resilient cloud services.

it.title: Gemini in Google Workspace can now connect directly to Salesforce, HubSpot, Asana, and more
it.summary: Google is rolling out MCP-based integrations that let Gemini interact directly with Salesforce, HubSpot, Asana, Monday, QuickBooks, Mailchimp, and Atlassian Rovo from Gmail, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Chat, and other Workspace apps. The important admin detail: third-party connectors are enabled by default for users with Gemini access, although IT can control them by domain, OU, or group, making this something Workspace admins should review rather than simply treat as another end-user AI feature.

it.title: Chrome 155 tightens enterprise restrictions on powerful extensions
it.summary: Starting with Chrome 155, extensions that use Chrome's powerful chrome.debugger API will be blocked from attaching when enterprise policies restrict host access, screenshots, or DLP-protected content. The change only affects managed browsers with those policies configured, but IT teams with internally developed or approved extensions should test ahead of the October 6 stable rollout because some extensions may stop working unless they move to more limited Chrome APIs.

it.title: Gartner: here's how AI will remake business in the next three years
it.summary: Gartner expects companies to face new operational problems ranging from AI “cost exhaustion” attacks to a flood of disposable AI-generated applications. One especially relevant prediction for IT: organizations will increasingly need real-time AI cost controls, while CIOs take greater responsibility for proving that governance and guardrails around AI actually exist and work.

it.title: Not every app in an enterprise is an enterprise app
it.summary: An application becomes an enterprise app based on business dependency rather than its technology, development speed, or where it is used. As AI coding agents enable employees to build software quickly, organizations must recognize that apps transition into enterprise software when the business relies on them to operate, requiring appropriate governance, support, and security as risks and user counts grow.

it.title: Teach Gemini your team's know-hows with skills in Google Workspace
it.summary: Google introduced reusable Workspace skills that package an organization's prompts, rules, templates, and reference material so Gemini can repeatedly follow the same process across Gmail, Docs, Drive, Chat, and Workspace Studio. Teams can collaborate on skills like documents, while centralized governance and Admin console distribution are coming, effectively turning internal procedures into reusable AI automations.

it.title: Introducing the New Salesforce Well-Architected Framework
it.summary: Salesforce has evolved its Well-Architected Framework to address the complexities of the Agentic Enterprise and interconnected autonomous systems. The updated framework is organized around five pillars: Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, Resource and Cost Optimization, and Fairness, each featuring a dedicated Agentic Enterprise lens.

it.title: Introducing Rivet BYOC
it.summary: Rivet has announced the release of Rivet BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud), a control plane deployed inside a customer's AWS or Google Cloud VPC and managed by Rivet. The offering allows data and compute to remain in the user's account while Rivet handles deployments, updates, and maintenance via an operator running in a Kubernetes cluster.

it.title: AIUC Raises $40 Million to Certify Enterprise AI Agents
it.summary: AIUC raised $40 million to expand a third-party testing and certification standard for enterprise AI agents, evaluating risks including prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, hallucinations, and unauthorized actions. The interesting part for IT and security teams is the emerging idea of a SOC 2-like independent assurance layer specifically for the agents companies are being asked to approve.

it.title: Dreamforce 2026 showed AI safety is the new big tech battleground
it.summary: Dreamforce put a growing disagreement among AI leaders on display, with Anthropic's Dario Amodei calling for stronger guardrails and a slower pace at the frontier while Nvidia's Jensen Huang argued against broadly slowing development. Regardless of which approach wins out, enterprises deploying agents will increasingly need their own standards for what models and capabilities they are willing to allow.

it.title: MCP Server Visibility
it.summary: Tracking Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers on employee devices is an endpoint inventory problem rather than an identity or network issue, because servers are launched locally via hand-edited configuration files without admin consoles or SSO logs. To maintain a complete inventory, security teams must read per-client configuration files across the fleet to resolve the actual entrypoints, package versions, and environment variables in use.

it.summary: This guide outlines the best knowledge engine platforms in 2026 and differentiates them from underlying components like vector databases and metadata catalogs.

it.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday inadvertently takes down copy and paste in Excel
it.summary: Microsoft's KB5002914 update can cause paste operations to silently fail in Excel 2016, 2019, 2021, and 2024.
